$comment: Why a counting rule changed, and whether the calibration window survived it.
Spec: docs/spec/the-ratchet.md. Decision: docs/adr/0085-a-renovation-is-declared-and-the-window-may-survive.md.
Ticket: https://github.com/mephistopheles4/stacks/issues/227
A STAMP RECORDS THE RULE A NUMBER WAS PRODUCED UNDER. When a stamp moves, numbers
either side of it are not comparable, so the calibration window restarts. Before this
file, nothing anywhere said WHY it moved: a reader of the trend page met a step change
and supplied their own story. The floors files carried dated prose, which marks the
FILE and never the series.
A STAMP ENTRY names one of configHash, fixtureHash or duplicationHash, and the value
that stamp took. G57 compares it to the floors file, so a stamp that moves without an
entry here is a RED PULL REQUEST rather than a surprise at the next deploy.
A FREE ENTRY says "stamp": "none". It records a change a reader notices and no stamp
records — a formatter adoption, a Node upgrade, a rule set widened. NOTHING CAN FORCE
A FREE ENTRY, because forcing means a comparison and there is no stamp to compare
against. That is a property of the class and not a gap in the gate. #227's own table
measured that Prettier, markdownlint and extra ESLint rules move no count, and #342
removed the last version trigger — so this class is now the only home for a renovation
a reader would otherwise have no record of.
AN UNRECOGNISED STAMP NAME IS A PARSE ERROR, which is parseCaps' rule in
scripts/lib/floors.ts for the same reason: a typo must not read as something weaker.
"fixturehash" would otherwise land as a free entry, leave the real stamp unmarked, and
pass the gate.
REQUIRED ON EVERY STAMP ENTRY AND NEVER DEFAULTED. It says whether the calibration
window survives this change. A default would let *nobody decided* read as *the window
restarts*, and this flag is the whole decision the marker exists to record.
true  — runs counted under the PREVIOUS value still count toward this stamp's window.
Claim it only when the counts themselves were measured unchanged.
false — the window restarts here, which is what a stamp change has always meant.
⚠️ IT IS READ FOR TWO STAMPS OF THE THREE. configHash and fixtureHash each have a
calibration window; duplicationHash has none, because the six duplication caps are #269's
and unbuilt. So `preserves` on a duplicationHash entry is required here and read by
nothing, and a `true` there would do nothing at all today. It is required anyway: a field
required on two stamps and forbidden on the third is a rule nobody remembers. WHOEVER
LANDS #269 WIRES acceptedValues(…, 'duplicationHash', …) INTO THAT WINDOW — nothing
reddens to remind them, which is the stated cost. See ADR-0085's Consequences.
⚠️ A JSCPD BUMP IS A BOT-CAUSED RENOVATION, and it is the only one left. duplicationHash
digests the jscpd version AS INSTALLED, because a clone detector's version decides what a
clone is — so a Dependabot pull request reddens G47 and G57 together and a bot can
re-derive neither. Accepted rather than answered: G47 already reddened that build, so the
human was already required. #328 and #339 are both that case.
THE THREE ENTRIES BELOW ARE ALL `false`, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN LAZY.
They are history, and ADR-0084 landed the same day saying records are not rewritten and
every window reads 0 of 10 from that commit. Seeding them `true` would silently reverse
an ADR one day old. The mechanism applies FORWARD.
APPEND ONLY, AND FILE ORDER IS THE RECORD. The newest entry for a stamp is the last one
naming it, read by position and never by date: two renovations can land on one day, and
a sort by date would pick between them by an accident of the sort's stability.

renovations.reason: G56 landed and the stamp was re-derived from the configuration it claims to describe. The scoring configuration itself did not move, so no score changed; the stamp did, because the gate that now compares it needed the file and the config to agree.
jscpd moved to 5.2.0. The installed version is an input to this stamp by design, because a clone detector's own version decides what a clone is. Measured across the bump: no duplication count moved.

The counting stamp stopped digesting the three installed versions and now holds the two rule-option sets and the two inventories. Measured: the same tree counted identically under two parser and eslint pairs, all 64 rows. This is the last version-driven refresh by construction — no dependency bump can move this stamp again.
